title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
An autonomous vehicle with a human safety operator struck and killed a duck in a residential neighborhood in Austin, Texas. The vehicle did not slow down or stop during the incident. This shows a failure in object detection or response, where the system either did not recognize a small moving animal as an obstacle, or recognized it but did not initiate collision avoidance.

The failure happened in a testing deployment on public streets with a human operator present. A human monitor could have intervened to stop or steer the vehicle had they detected the duck in time, suggesting the safety operator either did not see the hazard or did not have sufficient time to respond. It is not established whether the system's detection range, classification accuracy, or decision-making latency was the limiting factor.

A separate allegation that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign was disputed by the operator after reviewing data. This claim remains unverified and is distinct from the confirmed collision.

summary:
# Summary

An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. Residents were particularly upset because they knew the duck personally, as it had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant. Some neighbors also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this claim after reviewing vehicle data.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the car was operating in autonomous mode and stated it found no evidence supporting the stop sign allegation. The company has adjusted its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now evaluating technological improvements to prevent similar situations. Residents have recovered the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator. Several autonomous vehicle companies, including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox, currently operate or test vehicles in Austin.
